workLog.action: Measured the two invariants issue 3355 proposes across all 933 committed session logs before implementing either.
workLog.result: filename-stem to session.number holds 929/933. Branch-issue to session.number fails 207/276, in every month including 2026-07. The retrospective at .agents/retrospective/2026-07-26-pr-3354-session-log-churn.md reached the same conclusion independently, and review had already corrected its first draft on that exact point.

workLog.action: Implemented the filename invariant only, and documented in the docstring why the branch invariant was rejected.
workLog.result: Added filename_session_number() and validate_filename_number() to scripts/validate_session_json.py, wired into main(). validate_session_log() keeps its path-free contract so the 149 existing tests are untouched.

workLog.action: Corrected the two committed logs that violated the invariant, using neighbouring session numbers to decide which side was wrong.
workLog.result: Both took a session.number correction (9, 1711). Another candidate uses the legacy snake_case shape with no session object and is skipped by design.

workLog.action: Wrote 22 tests including a corpus test that runs the guard over every committed log.
workLog.result: 171 pass. The corpus test checks 930 logs with zero violations. The suite caught a real defect during authoring: the first regex read session-64a as 64, which would have failed six pre-convention logs; the digit run now has to end at a hyphen or the stem end.

Gutting the comparison turned 3 red. Reverting the regex boundary turned 2 red. Dropping the bool exclusion initially turned 0 red, which proved that test was not discriminating (True == 1 made a session-1 filename agree by coercion); the test was rewritten against a non-1 filename and the control then fired.

workLog.action: Verified the CLI path end to end.
workLog.result: A log named session-9999 carrying number 3371 exits 1 with the mismatch message. The same log under its correct name exits 0.

workLog.summary: Review caught the corpus guard silently skipping any log that failed to decode as UTF-8 or parse as JSON. The validator treats an unreadable log as a failure, so the skip meant a corrupt log could land while this test stayed green on the strength of its 900-sibling count. It now records the read failure as a violation naming the path, and the violation assertion runs before the count assertion so the specific message surfaces first.
